title: Opening the final session at the Hotel Chelsea, December 12, 1972
summary: Johnston opens the last session, describes the project and the earlier West Beth session, and sets the Chelsea location.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Opening the interview: introductions, date and place

blocks.x: This is Mrs. Armstead Johnston again beginning the final session of an extended interview with the arranger Gil Evans.

This interview is part of a jazz interactions project funded by the National Endowment for the Arts in Washington. Our last session, November 11th 1972 was held in the Evans' West Beth, that's WEST BETH at 463, West Street in Greenwich Village.

West Beth is a unique inner city colony of artists from all media. The building itself was formally the factory size research laboratory of Bell Telephone. Because it was, musicians like Gil Evans have spacious, loft type apartments with excellent acoustics.
Today's interview, Tuesday December 12th 1972 is being held in my apartment in the Hotel Chelsea on West 23rd Street. Built in 1894, it has long been famous as a residence for artists and scholars.
